title: AXI VALID/READY: Three Legal Timings and One Failure
description: Inspect each rising edge to distinguish an offered transfer, backpressure, an accepting handshake, and the illegal case where a source withdraws VALID before acceptance.

annotations.message: VALID-before-READY: the source offers payload A without waiting for READY. No transfer occurs because READY is LOW.
Backpressure continues. VALID and every payload/control bit must remain stable until an accepting edge.
READY becomes HIGH. Payload A transfers on this rising edge because VALID and READY are both HIGH.
READY-before-VALID: the destination advertises capacity, but no transfer occurs while VALID is LOW.
The source presents payload B. Because READY is already HIGH, B transfers immediately on this rising edge.
Neither side offers a transfer. VALID and READY may both be LOW.
Simultaneous assertion is legal. Payload C transfers on the first edge where both signals are HIGH.
The source offers payload D while READY is LOW. It has created an obligation to hold VALID and D stable.
Protocol error: the source withdrew VALID and payload D before a VALID-and-READY handshake accepted it.

violations.message: VALID dropped before handshake; the offered payload was never accepted.
